summary: Requires the Secretary of Energy, working with EPA and other agencies, to study and report to Congress within 18 months on how data centers affect communities of color and low-income communities through water and energy use, air and water pollution, grid impacts, jobs, taxes, property values, and public health risks, including a map of locations and recommendations for mitigation.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the Secretary of Energy (in coordination with other federal agencies) to conduct a study and issue a report within 18 months. This requires the allocation of federal administrative resources and personnel time, which constitutes a minor expansion of government activity and associated spending. No new appropriations or large-scale programs are authorized, so the effect is limited.

Section 3(b)(8) requires the study to examine effects on state and local tax revenue and tax incentives, but the bill itself makes no changes to tax policy, rates, or incentives. It is purely informational.
No provisions relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public health programs, or medical regulation.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration policy, border security, visas, or immigrant protections.
No provisions address reproductive rights, abortion access, or related regulations.
No provisions address military, defense, or national security spending or policy.

The bill's findings and required study explicitly focus on data centers' energy and water consumption, air emissions, wastewater impacts, land use, and public-health risks, with particular attention to environmental justice in communities of color and low-income areas. It directs recommendations for federal coordination and best practices to mitigate harms. This engages environmental protection and regulation themes, though only through study rather than new mandates.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, housing subsidies, or related safety-net policies.
No provisions address schools, education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance-abuse programs.
No provisions address policing, sentencing, incarceration, or criminal-justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The bill implies negligible new federal spending for a one-time study; it does not engage with deficit spending, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights issues.
No provisions address foreign aid, international assistance, or related funding.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or voter-ID requirements.

The bill examines data-center energy, water, and environmental impacts but does not address data privacy, cybersecurity, content moderation, or tech-platform regulation. Any link to tech oversight is indirect and minimal.
Section 3(b)(7) requires examination of job creation and displacement effects, but the bill contains no provisions altering labor law, union rights, or employer obligations.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil-rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination rules.
